predecessors.name: Greek city-states (independent poleis)
predecessors.text: Athens reached out to Aegean cities under harsh Spartan control including Chios, Byzantium, Rhodes, and Mytilene; the league 'included over 60 states'

successors.name: Greek city-states (independent poleis)
successors.text: Attica and the islands Athens kept; 'the Athenians were allowed to keep their colony on Samos'

ledger.x: 378: Athens founds the Second Athenian League.
377: Chios, Rhodes, Kos and Byzantion are among the founding allies.
377: Euboea is a member of the league.
377: the league's other Aegean and Thracian members join.
ledger.cp: Allied cities that became independent in 355

ledger.x: 377: the members that Athens kept after 355 join.
ledger.cp: Allied cities that stayed with Athens

ledger.x: 360: Cotys I's Odrysians take the Thracian Chersonese from Athens.
357: Cersobleptes cedes the Thracian Chersonese to Athens.
357: the Social War opens at Chios.
355: Athens makes peace and accepts its allies' independence.
355: Chios, Rhodes, Kos and Byzantion leave the league for good ('Confederate allies independent' in the infobox).
355: the league ends in all but name.
ledger.cp: Allied cities that became independent in 355

ledger.x: 355: Chios, Rhodes, Kos and Byzantion return to the Greek aggregate as independent cities (mirror of the Greek-city-states gain at -355).
355: the other members that left become independent cities of the Greek aggregate; the region is the researcher's reading of 'most of the allied cities'.
350: Euboea is again on Athens's side.
338: Chalcis takes a Macedonian garrison after Chaeronea.

ledger.cp: Allied cities that stayed with Athens

ledger.x: 338: Attica and the rump of the league pass to the Macedonian-led Greek states.
338: Chaeronea ends the Second Athenian League.

wars.name: Social War (357-355 BC)
wars.outcome: The four allies broke away and Athens recognised their independence in 355; most of the allied cities left the league.

wars.name: Struggle for the Thracian Chersonese
wars.outcome: Cersobleptes ceded the peninsula to Athens in 357; Athenian settlers arrived in 353.

wars.name: Battle of Chaeronea (338 BC)
wars.outcome: Macedonian victory; the Second Athenian League was dissolved and Athens kept Samos.
